questions.subject: en
questions.passage: Nigar lives on the ninth floor of a tall building in Baku, so she has no garden. Two years ago she decided to grow vegetables on her balcony. She started with tomatoes and herbs in old plastic boxes. At first, most of the plants died because they got too much sun in the afternoon. Nigar read about the problem and moved the boxes to the shady side of the balcony. She also began to water them early in the morning instead of in the evening. Now her balcony is full of green leaves, and her family eats fresh salad almost every day. Last spring Nigar showed her neighbours how to start their own balcony gardens.
questions.text: Why did Nigar start growing vegetables on her balcony?
questions.explanation: Mətndə deyilir: doqquzuncu mərtəbədə yaşadığı üçün bağı yoxdur.

questions.subject: en
questions.passage: Every Saturday a big blue bus stops in the centre of a small village near Shamakhi. It is not an ordinary bus — it is a library on wheels. Inside, there are shelves with about two thousand books, two computers and a small table for children. The village has no library of its own, so the bus is very popular. People can borrow up to three books for two weeks. The driver, Mr Rauf, is also the librarian. He says that the most popular books are adventure stories for teenagers and cookery books for adults. In winter, when the roads are icy, the bus sometimes cannot come, and the villagers say they really miss it.
questions.text: What is special about the blue bus?

questions.subject: en
questions.passage: The robotics club at School No. 47 meets twice a week after lessons. This year twelve students are preparing for a national competition in which robots must find their way through a maze. The team's first robot was fast but kept hitting the walls. The students then added two extra sensors, which made the robot slower but much more accurate. Their teacher, Ms Leyla, does not write any code for them. She only asks questions and helps them test their ideas. 'When the robot fails, we learn the most,' says Murad, the youngest member of the team. The competition will take place in March, and the club is now looking for a sponsor to pay for new parts.
questions.text: What must the robots do in the competition?
options: find their way through a maze
questions.explanation: «…robots must find their way through a maze.»

questions.subject: en
questions.passage: Camels are well suited to life in the desert. Contrary to a popular belief, a camel's hump does not hold water. It stores fat, which the animal can use for energy when there is little food. Camels can go for many days without drinking, and when they finally find water, they can drink a very large amount in a few minutes. Their long eyelashes and the ability to close their noses protect them from sand during storms. Wide, soft feet help them walk on hot sand without sinking. Because of these features, people in desert regions have used camels for transport for thousands of years.
questions.text: What does a camel's hump store?

questions.subject: en
questions.passage: Scientists say that teenagers need between eight and ten hours of sleep every night, but many get much less. One reason is that the body clock changes during the teenage years, so young people naturally feel sleepy later in the evening. Another reason is the use of phones and tablets in bed. The light from screens tells the brain that it is still daytime. Lack of sleep can make it harder to concentrate, remember new information and control emotions. Doctors advise teenagers to go to bed at the same time every day, to keep their phones out of the bedroom and to avoid drinks with caffeine in the evening.
questions.text: How many hours of sleep do teenagers need?

questions.subject: en
questions.passage: The Palace of the Shaki Khans is one of the most famous historical buildings in Azerbaijan. It was built in the 18th century as a summer residence for the rulers of Shaki. The palace is not very large, but it is famous for its colourful wall paintings and its shebeke windows. Shebeke is a traditional art in which small pieces of coloured glass are fitted into a wooden frame without nails or glue. When sunlight passes through the windows, the rooms fill with red, blue and green light. Today the palace is a museum, and tourists from many countries visit it every year.
questions.text: When was the palace built?
